newsitem.title: USA: CME hog, pork belly futures end lower on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hog, pork belly futures end lower on weak cash.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures closed lower, pressured by selling from traders believing there will not be an immediate recovery in either cash hog or pork prices, traders said.

Commodity funds were the leading sellers in the hog pit, exiting long positions, traders said. Scattered short covering throughout the session slowed declines in February, but was less a factor in April which closed down 1.100 cents at 73.700 cents per lb.
Traders throughout the day said bearish fundamental factors weighed on futures.

Cash hog prices were lower Thursday and were expected at least $0.50 per cwt lower Friday. Meat packers, with margins pinched by falling pork prices, will need only a few hogs to satisfy an expected small Saturday slaughter.

USDA reported pork cutout values were down $0.11 to $0.14 per cwt late Wednesday, and USDA's carlot pork report released at midday Thursday indicated cash ham and trimmings prices were under pressure.
In the pork belly pit, storage interests were noted selling February, while locals were leading sellers of the March, traders said.

Hogs closed down 1.100 to 0.050 cent per lb with February off 0.475 at 75.025 cents and March was off 1.100 at 73.700. Pork bellies closed down 1.00 to 0.500 cent per lb with February off the most at 76.325 cents and March was off 0.600 at 75.850.
